# About
I like to think of myself as part metacommunity ecologist, part open science enthusiast, with a soft spot for open ecosystems. I’m happiest when I get to learn, teach, and figure things out with other people.

I’m a Latina from Brazil, so we can absolutely talk in Portuguese! I’m also happy to chat in English. I can read and understand spoken French, but speaking it is still a little adventure — one I’m happy to try!

## How I got here

I got my BSc in Biology (2021) and MSc in Ecology, Evolution and Biodiversity (2024) at Universidade Estadual Paulista (UNESP), in Rio Claro, Brazil. In 2025, I also worked there as a research technician, helping with data management for the [Cerrado On Fire](https://bv.fapesp.br/pt/bolsas/224767/implementacao-de-um-banco-de-dados-sobre-dados-ecologicos-de-comunidades-de-plantas-sob-manejo-de-fo/) project.

My interest in disturbance ecology started during my undergraduate studies, when I [studied](https://repositorio.unesp.br/server/api/core/bitstreams/8201fbe9-6338-4035-9833-f5ffc20c051f/content) beta diversity across communities under different fire regimes. I also explored how biological invasion and fire interact to shape plant communities, which led to [my first publication](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/jvs.13250).

Working with the herbaceous layer of the Cerrado, still the most beautiful biome in the world, helped grow my love for vegetation ecology. These days, my PhD questions take me beyond fire: I’m interested in how novel disturbance regimes shape biodiversity across time, space, and levels of ecological organization.

## The science I want to help build

Also, I could happily spend a long time talking about open science, FAIR principles, and good data practices. 
As an OS instructor, I also want to make room for questions, practice, and learning together. These interests keep bringing me back to a question: what kind of science are we really trying to do? And what kind of academic culture makes it possible? I care about what we discover, but also about how we get there, whose voices are heard, and how we treat one another along the way. I want to help build spaces where people feel welcome, supported, and able to ask questions without having to prove they belong. To me, equity and mental well-being aren’t extras, they’re part of the science culture we need to build.

You don’t need to have a project in mind to say hello. If you’d like to exchange ideas, ask a question, or figure something out together, [I’d be happy to hear from you](mailto:gabriela.dezotti@unesp.br).
